item.title: Melatonin: The Hormone Bomb in Your Medicine Cabinet — Evidence Score 6/10
item.description:
Seventy million Americans take melatonin. Most are taking ten times the clinical dose, at the wrong time, for the wrong reason. Zara breaks down what the research actually shows about melatonin efficacy, the alarming new heart failure data from a 130,000-person observational study, and the one population where the evidence is genuinely strong. No supplement deals. Just the science.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Topic Frame 02:00 — Segment 1 07:00 — Segment 2 13:00 — Segment 3 16:00 — The Verdict
Sources cited in this episode: • Ferracioli-Oda et al. meta-analysis (19 RCTs, n=1,683) — melatonin reduced sleep onset latency by ~7 • Nnadi et al. (SUNY Downstate, presented AHA Scientific Sessions 2025) — TriNetX observational study, • Analysis of 34 melatonin supplements — only 22-48% met label claims within 10% margin; absorption in • RCT on REM sleep behavior disorder — 2 mg nightly for 6 months reduced symptom severity by ~50% in f • Multicenter RCT (melatonin 3 mg vs. amitriptyline 25 mg vs. placebo, 12 weeks) — equivalent ~50% mig
Next episode: Next time: CBT-I — cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia. It outperforms sleep medication in head-to-head trials. So why does almost nobody use it? We're getting into that.
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast. Our hosts hold zero financial positions and have zero sponsors.
